output.brief:
The rejects come from one specific combination: Arnholt resin dried in Press 5's dryer (D5), which has been running wet. Press 5 with Arnholt rejects about 10% of parts on both shifts. Press 5 with Quillan is about 0.9%. Press 7 with either resin is under 1%. Arnholt arrives wetter than Quillan, and D5 can't dry it enough. The same Arnholt lot dried in a good portable dryer gave 0.8% rejects. The second shift looks worse only because all its VX runs on Press 5. New and experienced operators perform identically, so don't discipline the six new operators. Dropping Arnholt isn't needed either.

Next steps this week: repair D5 (heater and desiccant) and verify it reaches −40 °C. Restore the alarm limit. Keep Arnholt off D5 until then, by sending it to Press 7 or drying it in a verified dryer. Add a feed-throat moisture check for every resin lot. Ask Arnholt why its resin arrives wetter than Quillan. I'm fairly confident in the main diagnosis. The one open question is whether storing resin in the north annex adds moisture. Every Arnholt sample came from the annex, so that is untested. Don't pay for outside storage until it is checked.
